key_insight: GrimAge acceleration was the only DNA methylation age measure consistently associated with higher all-cause dementia risk, while overall findings across neurodegenerative diseases were limited and inconsistent.
clinical_relevance: Current evidence is insufficient to support DNA methylation clocks as neurodegenerative disease biomarkers; this paper does not address AI-driven cancer drug discovery.
method: Systematic review across six databases of DNA methylation age metrics and neurodegenerative diseases.
Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects meta-analyses with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment.
Included observational and Mendelian randomization studies.
evidence_signal: Across 37 observational studies involving 46,365 participants and seven Mendelian randomization studies, longitudinal pooling linked higher GrimAge acceleration to dementia risk (HR per SD 1.11, 95% CI 1.02–1.20).
watch_item: Causal evidence was limited, and disease-specific clocks require development and independent validation before potential clinical use.
paper_title: Biological age measured by DNA methylation clocks and neurodegenerative diseases: A systematic review and meta-analysis
